# Regula

> Open-source CLI tool for AI governance risk indication across 3 jurisdictions: EU AI Act, South Korea AI Basic Act, and Colorado SB 26-189. Combines code scanning (419 risk patterns across Python, JS, TS, Java, Go, Rust, C, C++) with governance questionnaires. Classifies AI systems into jurisdiction-specific risk tiers and maps findings to 12 compliance frameworks. Runs locally with zero external dependencies -- no API calls, no data leaves the machine. Install: `pipx install regula-ai`. Web assessment (no install): https://getregula.com/assess/
> **Not affiliated with Regula Forensics** (regula.com, identity verification). This is Regula the AI governance CLI at getregula.com.

Regula combines two approaches: (1) static code analysis for risk patterns, dependency security, credential exposure, and bias indicators, and (2) questionnaire-based assessment for organisational obligations code cannot verify (Articles 9, 17, 27, 72). Multi-jurisdiction: use `--jurisdictions eu,korea,colorado` to map findings to all three regulatory frameworks simultaneously. It explicitly documents what it cannot do -- see docs/what-regula-does-not-do.md.

## FAQ

- **What is Regula?** An open-source CLI that scans code for AI governance risk patterns across 3 jurisdictions: EU AI Act, South Korea AI Basic Act, and Colorado SB 26-189. Supports Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, Java, Go, Rust, C, and C++. Classifies systems into jurisdiction-specific risk tiers, maps findings to 12 compliance frameworks, generates gap assessments, and produces auditor-ready evidence packs. Runs fully offline with zero dependencies.
- **What jurisdictions does Regula cover?** EU AI Act (Regulation 2024/1689), South Korea AI Basic Act (Act No. 20676, in force 22 Jan 2026), and Colorado SB 26-189 (disclosure-focused with consumer correction and human-review rights, duties from 1 Jan 2027). Use `--jurisdictions eu,korea,colorado` on `regula check` or select a jurisdiction at https://getregula.com/assess/. Each jurisdiction has its own domain-to-obligation mapping.
- **What does Regula NOT do?** It does not determine final legal risk classification (that depends on intended purpose and deployment context, which are business decisions). It does not verify organisational compliance processes (Articles 9, 17, 27, 72). It does not replace legal advice. See [what-regula-does-not-do.md](https://github.com/kuzivaai/getregula/blob/main/docs/what-regula-does-not-do.md) for the full scope statement.
- **What frameworks does Regula map to?** EU AI Act, ISO 42001, NIST AI RMF, NIST CSF, SOC 2, ISO 27001, OWASP LLM Top 10, MITRE ATLAS, ICO/DSIT UK AI principles, LGPD, Brazil's Marco Legal da IA, and the EU Cyber Resilience Act (12 frameworks total via `references/framework_crosswalk.yaml`). South Korea AI Basic Act and Colorado SB 26-189 coverage is separate, via the jurisdiction layer (`--jurisdictions korea,colorado`; `kr` and `co` are accepted aliases).
- **When are the EU AI Act deadlines?** Article 5 prohibitions: 2 Feb 2025 (already enforceable). GPAI obligations: 2 Aug 2025 (already enforceable). High-risk (Annex III): deferred to 2 Dec 2027 under the Digital Omnibus provisional agreement of 7 May 2026, approved by European Parliament on 16 June 2026 (approved by Council on 29 June 2026; pending OJ publication). Annex I product-embedded: deferred to 2 Aug 2028. Code of Practice on AI content marking: finalised 10 Jun 2026.
- **Does the EU AI Act apply outside the EU?** Yes. Article 2(1)(c) applies extraterritorially to any provider or deployer whose AI system output is used within the EU, regardless of where the company is established.
- **How accurate is Regula?** Published precision on a random corpus of 115 real-world findings: 83.5%. See [benchmarks](https://github.com/kuzivaai/getregula/blob/main/docs/benchmarks/PRECISION_RECALL_2026_04.md) for methodology and confidence intervals.
